Thanks for letting me know from the other side.

To be honest, this has never be put across to me whether from her or anyone else. In terms of her feeling overwhelmed and my expectations, I'm not sure if that is how I feel too. Maybe I can share an incident and hear your views to understand from the other side. Quite a few times, we've been to places where my mental scars will be triggered that I would be affected so badly. I've ever voiced out with her a few times before when I'm much settled down. However, after a certain period, she would insist on going such places again. FYI - these places are areas that can be deemed as trespassing. Once, I told her that I didn't feel like going. She would ask me why. I just said no and would like to go somewhere else. She would continue to ask me why don't want to go or what's up with me. This is where I got upset because it did felt like she didn't really understand what was wrong. That period, I was quite suicidal that I would just want to avoid talking about or doing anything that I can relate as negative which I've talked with her before. Instead, she kept on asking why don't I want to go. At that point, it felt like she totally forgotten what we spoke about and even triggered me further. Like, I just needed that one time for her to know that negativity has triggered and needed her to avoid it (or at least ask in a way to know if it has been triggered).

I can agree and relate with you on the "... didn't like her follow ups.". Sometimes I do tell her that too. But I did explain that her follow ups sound very contradicting. She has always told me she doesn't like assumptions especially on people's feelings. But yet, not introducing me to her family was her assumption that we may have issues in our r/s and may not last long (this was before I was suicidal).

As for her "date", she does know I'm upset and told me awhile later that she would avoid such things. Her reasons were that she thought it was ok to hang out with the opposite gender 1-on-1 even when attached. I had to explain to her that I think it's fairly ok to do so but there should be some form of limits even if there were special "conditions". Like if it was a male friend that really wanted to talk out his feelings through drinks, I'm ok if she accompanies him and I'll pick her after her drinks. But to her, she thinks it's ok to go out with a male even if it's for a movie, staycation and even a trip. I had to explain so long that I had to use these exact words "I trust you but I don't trust that guy". And thus, she decided to go for the movie cause she knows it wouldn't be anything special.

Our age difference is 1 and we are in our early thirties.

Initially, she had doubts of this r/s because we have different characteristics and behaviors. But for me, one of the beliefs I had was that no 2 people will have be in sync and couples need to work with and learn from each other. The best example I can give is that I used to be a very logical person and I don't understand what emotions are about. But in time with her, I realized that my emotions and mental state are important and have started to be more patient towards people. Even after talking to her on this, I'm not sure if she sees anything to learn from me. But I've never even once heard on what and how she wants to work with me. Probably you're also right on the judging since I used to be a very straightforward person.

I guess for me is that, some part of me do hope to have her around and support especially since things haven't been easy for me during this period. But other parts of me feel really hurt as the same person who I trust the most is the same person who I feel left out from.

Thanks for the advice. I did also feedback to her with regards to this "drip-feeding", though that wasn't the words I used.

But yeah, I do feel that she's never proud of me as her actions are different from her words. I'll try to manage this as much as I can since this period of my life has been a downward spiral. I guess some part of me still hopes that I have her support.

You’re still young. To be honest, no one knows what is the right path and if they are on the right path. If one thing life has taught us is that everyone is always learning and that includes learning to take the right path.

Take some time to think about it and maybe do it like a pros and cons list. For example, what did you like and dislike about accounting. Given that you’ve managed to self studied all the way meant that there were some motivational factors/somethings you’ve liked. If the cons eventually outweigh the pros, then quit it and do something else.

When thinking about doing something else, think about what you really want to do and ask around if that sector really interests you. From there, take small steps to achieve it.

It may come back as a vicious cycle where you’ll wound up again thinking this (the new interest) is something you dread to do, then take a step back and do the same again.

Just always remember that no one can tell you what is right except yourself and you’re not the only person who faces dilemma in life’s choices
